steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: from map coordinates to a bounded result
steps.detail: NearbyDiscoveryController exposes /api/v1/discovery/kitchens and /menu-items. Read the method signature carefully: latitude and longitude are BigDecimal inputs, radiusMeters is an explicit integer, and filters include query, category, food type, price bounds, preparation time and spice level. Sort, page and size also affect the result. The controller constructs DiscoveryCriteria and delegates the actual discovery to NearbyDiscoveryService. PostGIS adds spatial operations to PostgreSQL; it does not decide Craves' commercial serviceability policy. Trace the controller into the spatial query and record the coordinate system and distance units used there. A small bounding box and an exact distance predicate answer different questions. Do not replace the existing query with a frontend approximation or assume kilometers where the contract says meters.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: wrong location, wrong cache or no meals
steps.detail: An empty page can result from location, radius, active status, filters or pagination; it is not automatically a backend outage. Reproduce with a synthetic coordinate and change one filter at a time. The reviewed controller constructs a cache key from the response kind, privacy mode, location, radius, filter values, sort and pagination. Explain why leaving one of those dimensions out could return another request's result. Code supporting caching is not evidence that the production cache flag is enabled. Keep the currently deployed flag unchanged during an Academy exercise. Never increase a delivery radius or expose exact home-kitchen coordinates merely to populate a demo screen.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: build a discovery investigation matrix
steps.detail: Create twelve synthetic requests covering the two discovery routes, two sort modes, an empty page, changed radius, changed food type and changed privacy mode. Map every request dimension to the controller, criteria and cache-key input. Read PublicCatalogControllerPrivacyTest and run mvn -B -ntp -f services/catalog-service/pom.xml -Dtest=PublicCatalogControllerPrivacyTest,InternalCatalogAuthorizerTest test. These tests are targeted privacy/internal-access checks, not a spatial load test. For database investigation, use a disposable PostGIS database and EXPLAIN on a representative query; EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query and is not automatically safe on production. Record plan, row estimates and test dataset size without claiming production capacity.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a request-to-query map, cache-dimension matrix and correctly scoped test report. Explain the difference between valid coordinates, discovery radius and approved delivery coverage.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: track facts and units across boundaries
steps.detail: Read the menu request and response definitions used by CatalogService rather than guessing field names from a card on the screen. For every package or portion attribute, identify its data type, unit, nullability, validation and authoritative source. Distinguish a menu's serving description from the physical package information required by an external delivery adapter. A customer-facing portion estimate does not justify inventing a dispatch weight or dimensions. Follow the approved facts from chef entry through Catalog storage and public DTO, then identify which must be copied into an order or delivery request. The training task is to document the existing contract and its gaps, not to fill missing physical facts with arbitrary defaults.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: historical and public representations
steps.detail: A menu can change after an order is placed. Ask whether each downstream value is read live or preserved at transaction time, and show the actual owner of that decision. Avoid silently recalculating a historical order using today's menu metadata. Public images also have a privacy boundary: the reviewed privacy test keeps a public image URL while redacting internal blob-container and blob-name fields. A storage coordinate is not a required customer-visible attribute just because it appears in an internal DTO. When extending package metadata, inspect every public mapper and internal consumer, not only the persistence column.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: produce a complete field-lineage sheet
steps.detail: Choose three existing menu attributes from the DTO and trace each through validation, service mapping, repository schema, public response and a consuming client. Add a synthetic omitted-value and invalid-unit case to your worksheet. Use the publicMenuImageRedactsBlobStorageCoordinates test as a concrete example of a representation boundary: explain each assertion and add one training-only assertion that guards against an additional private field leaking. Run the focused Catalog tests. Submit the field-lineage sheet with exact source paths and a gap column. A blank or unknown unit must remain an identified requirement gap rather than becoming a guessed number.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: field lineage with explicit units and ownership, public/private response distinctions, and one regression assertion. No menu, price, package rule or provider configuration is changed in production.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: separate public discovery from internal fulfillment
steps.detail: PublicCatalogController and NearbyDiscoveryController serve customer-discovery representations; an internal order consumer may require protected pickup or ownership data that must not be exposed publicly. PublicCatalogControllerPrivacyTest deliberately exercises both activated privacy behavior and a staged compatibility mode. That duality is an important release dependency: a privacy toggle can change a contract needed by an older internal consumer. Read the internal authorizer and the Order service's CatalogClientInternalAccessTest before deciding the consumer has migrated. The existence of an internal endpoint alone is not proof that every caller uses it. Trace each caller to its actual URL and credential mechanism at the pinned source revision.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: a successful response may still be unsafe
steps.detail: A 200 response containing a private pickup address is not a privacy success. Conversely, a sanitized public response may be insufficient for internal fulfillment, and substituting it can break chef-order processing. Document two distinct DTO contracts and test their field presence rather than treating one large shared response as convenient. InternalCatalogAuthorizerTest covers configured internal credentials, a wrong credential without echoing the expected value, and fail-closed behavior when the binding is missing. Do not bypass that check by making an internal route public. Never paste the expected internal credential into a regression test or training guide.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: create a caller-contract dependency map
steps.detail: List public web/mobile discovery, chef-management and internal order callers as separate entries. For each, record path, authentication, allowed data, forbidden data, owner and compatibility dependency. Read the active and staged-mode privacy tests and explain why their expectations differ. Add a synthetic test case showing that the public representation does not include exact private location details when privacy enforcement is active. Review the Order internal-client tests without running any live service request. Deliver a two-phase migration plan: first prove internal consumers use the protected contract, then separately approve the public privacy activation. The exercise must not flip a runtime flag.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: the caller map, positive and negative privacy assertions, and an activation plan that recognizes source availability is different from completed consumer migration.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: add an optional descriptive field locally
steps.detail: Training-only feature brief: add an optional plain-text serving note to a synthetic menu representation without changing price, availability, dietary claims or delivery calculation. Locate the actual request/response definitions and CatalogService mapping first. Write a field contract stating maximum length, omitted/null/empty behavior and which existing authorized actor may edit it. Those constraints belong to the training brief and must not be mistaken for an approved Craves product rule. Identify whether persistence is needed; if it is, create a new additive migration in the training branch instead of editing an applied one. Trace the field through internal and public mappers and the selected client parser.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: adding one field affects many readers
steps.detail: Plan success, overlong input, unauthorized writer, omitted old-row value and an older client that ignores the new field. Use plain text rendering; do not treat a chef-entered string as executable HTML. Do not make a formerly optional field required on every existing menu row without a migration and product decision. Check any cached discovery representation for invalidation or deliberate exclusion of the new field. A migration test on an empty database cannot prove compatibility with existing menus, so create an old-shape synthetic fixture. If an order needs the note historically, that is a separate explicit Order contract change, not a live Catalog lookup hidden in an invoice.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: demonstrate the complete field path
steps.detail: Create training/catalog-serving-note locally. Write request-validation and response-mapping tests before implementing the field. Use synthetic menu data only. Implement the necessary DTO/service/persistence changes, then a runtime client parser and a small presentation component that tolerates absence. Run the relevant Java tests, TypeScript tests and build/typecheck for the selected client. Add a privacy assertion that existing redaction still holds. Submit a file tree, complete changed files, before/after JSON, migration compatibility evidence and a rollback note. Do not publish the training branch, run a chef mutation against production or deploy Catalog as part of Academy publication.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: the local vertical slice with absent-value compatibility and privacy tests. The reviewer must be able to follow the field from input to screen and explain whether historical orders should or should not receive it.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: performance evidence needs a workload
steps.detail: A discovery endpoint's capacity depends on query shape, active dataset, indexes, cache behavior, connection limits and response size. Record workload assumptions before measuring latency. Use representative synthetic spatial distributions instead of ten identical rows. Distinguish cold-cache and warm-cache behavior, and measure high-percentile latency and error rates rather than only an average. Inspect the query plan before proposing more replicas. The current one-replica operating posture is an explicit constraint, not evidence that a million simultaneous users have been supported. Training may identify a capacity risk; it must not silently provision paid infrastructure or enable caching to make a benchmark look faster.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: isolate contract, data and performance regressions
steps.detail: For a bad discovery release, compare the failing request and response with the previous version, then inspect filter normalization, cache dimensions, privacy mode, query plan and data eligibility. If only a new client mapper is wrong, do not roll back other backend services. If cached data is stale, use the approved invalidation/recovery mechanism rather than changing the source record repeatedly. Preserve current migrations and transactional history. Record whether the previous application can read the new optional column before a code rollback. A source code fix and a production incident closure need distinct evidence.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: design a bounded performance and release gate
steps.detail: Prepare a nonproduction test plan with exact synthetic row counts, coordinate distribution, request mix, concurrency, duration, latency/error thresholds and abort conditions chosen for the exercise. Run the focused privacy and internal-access tests and record that they do not replace load testing. Add old/new DTO compatibility and representative query-plan evidence to the release packet. Specify the exact image/revision rollback point and checks for preserved flags, secret references and one-replica settings. Mark all live capacity and authenticated smoke fields pending unless actually observed. Do not run a load generator against craves.in, the production gateway or a delivery provider.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a reproducible nonproduction workload definition, honest executed/not-executed results and a narrow recovery plan. No production capacity guarantee can be inferred from curriculum completion or a passing unit test.
